population.text: Patients with toxic plasma methotrexate concentrations (>1 micromol/L) and severely delayed methotrexate clearance due to renal dysfunction

endpoint.text: Proportion of patients achieving a rapid (≤ 15 minutes) and sustained (≥ 8 days) clinically important reduction (RSCIR) in plasma methotrexate concentration, defined as attainment of plasma methotrexate ≤ 1 micromol/L at 15 minutes sustained for up to 8 days

citations.quote: The main outcome measure was the proportion of patients who achieved a rapid and sustained clinically important reduction (RSCIR) in plasma methotrexate concentration, defined as an attainment of plasma methotrexate concentration \le 1 \mu\text{mol/L} at 15 minutes that was sustained for up to 8 days following the initial injection.

n.text: FDA per-protocol efficacy population of 22 patients (applicant assessment based on 27 patients)

citations.quote: No. of Patients	22	27

result.text: 10 of 22 patients achieved RSCIR [45% (95% CI 27, 65)]; all 22 patients had ≥ 97% reduction in plasma methotrexate within 15 minutes

citations.quote: Ten of the 22 patients achieved RSCIR [45% (95% CI 27, 65%)].
with reduction in plasma methotrexate concentration by \ge 97\% within 15 minutes in all 22 patients.

indication.text: Treatment of toxic plasma methotrexate concentrations (>1 micromole per liter) in patients with delayed methotrexate clearance due to impaired renal function

citations.quote: VORAXAZE (glucarpidase) is indicated for the treatment of toxic plasma methotrexate concentrations (>1 micromole per liter) in patients with delayed methotrexate clearance due to impaired renal function.

target_moa.text: Glucarpidase is a bacterial carboxypeptidase enzyme that hydrolyzes methotrexate to two inactive metabolites (DAMPA and glutamate), rapidly reducing plasma methotrexate concentrations

citations.quote: a bacterial enzyme that hydrolyzes methotrexate to produce two inactive metabolites (DAMPA and glutamate)
Glucarpidase is a homodimeric, carboxypeptidase enzyme with a molecular weight of 83 kDa.

modality.text: enzyme (recombinant carboxypeptidase enzyme produced by genetically-modified E. coli)

citations.quote: It is produced by a genetically-modified *E. coli* containing the gene for carboxypeptidase cloned from *Pseudomonas* straing Rs-16.
Drug Class:	Recombinant Enzyme

key_safety.text: Among 290 patients in the safety evaluation, 21 (7%) had VORAXAZE-related adverse reactions, mostly Grade 1 or 2; most common (>1%) were paresthesias (2%), flushing (2%), nausea/vomiting (2%), headache (1%) and hypotension (1%). Serious allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, occurred in less than 1% of patients.

citations.quote: Twenty-one of 290 patients (7%) experienced adverse reactions that were assessed as related to VORAXAZE. Most were Grade 1 or 2 events.

summary.text: Voraxaze received Fast Track designation (granted 1/5/2007) and was submitted as a rolling review, with the final portion completed on July 18, 2011. The BLA was granted Priority review and approved on a traditional (full) approval basis. Orphan drug exclusivity was granted for the indication. The application was not referred to an advisory committee.
